hints: Focus on Le Chatelier's principle here, the system will shift to oppose any change in pressure or temperature.
Count the moles of gas on each side, you have 2 moles on the left and 4 moles on the right.
Notice the forward reaction is endothermic with positive delta H, so think about which temperature pushes an endothermic change forward.
walkthrough:
**Count the gas moles for pressure**

Think of pressure as squeezing the gases together. The equilibrium shifts to the side with fewer gas molecules to relieve the squeeze.

Left side: $$1 + 1 = 2 \text{ mol gas}$$
Right side: $$1 + 3 = 4 \text{ mol gas}$$

**Apply Le Chatelier for pressure**

To make more hydrogen we need to shift right, toward 4 moles. That is favoured by low pressure, because low pressure favours the side with more moles of gas.

**Use delta H for temperature**

The forward reaction has $\Delta H^{o} = +205 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, so it is endothermic. It takes in heat as it goes forward.

$$\text{CH}_{4}(g) + \text{H}_{2}\text{O}(g) \rightleftharpoons \text{CO}(g) + 3\text{H}_{2}(g) \quad \Delta H > 0$$

**Choose the best pair**

High temperature adds heat, so the system uses it up by shifting right in the endothermic direction. Low pressure plus high temperature together give the maximum yield of hydrogen.

options.A: High temperature is correct for this endothermic reaction, but high pressure is wrong. High pressure shifts equilibrium left toward only 2 moles of gas, reducing hydrogen yield.
options.B: Both parts are wrong for maximum yield. High pressure favours the left (fewer moles) and low temperature favours the exothermic backward reaction, both decrease hydrogen.
options.C: This is correct. Low pressure favours the side with more gas moles (4 moles on the right), and high temperature favours the endothermic forward reaction. Both shift equilibrium right to make more $\text{H}_{2}$.
options.D: Low pressure is correct, but low temperature is wrong. Low temperature favours the exothermic direction, which here is the backward reaction, so hydrogen yield falls.
